title: Redirects as Routing: From URL to Function — Check

questions.prompt: Why does the redirect use `status = 200` instead of `301` or `302`?
questions.explanation: Status 200 makes it a transparent rewrite: the edge proxies to the function while the client still sees /agronomy-api/, hiding the implementation path.
options: To force the browser to cache the response
To rewrite the request server-side so the client keeps the original URL
Because 200 is required for all Netlify functions
To make the request faster by skipping the function

questions.prompt: In the rule `to = "/.netlify/functions/agronomy-api/:splat"`, what does `:splat` represent?
questions.explanation: `:splat` carries forward the portion matched by the `*` wildcard, so subpaths are preserved through the rewrite.
options: Whatever the `*` wildcard in the `from` pattern matched

questions.prompt: Because the rewrite keeps the API on the same origin as the app, typical cross-origin CORS handling is largely unnecessary.
questions.explanation: The browser sees /agronomy-api on the same origin, so the gateway call is not cross-origin and CORS friction is avoided.
